items.title: Wishart law by Gaussian outer products
items.statement: Assume AC. For integers $p,m\ge1$ and a real symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix $\Sigma$, define $W_p(\Sigma,m)$ as the pushforward of the finite product law $N_p(0,\Sigma)^{\otimes m}$ by $(z_1,\ldots,z_m)\mapsto\sum_{j=1}^m z_jz_j^T$. This convention allows singular support when $m<p$ or $\Sigma$ is singular; no density is asserted.
items.strategy: Define the law as the pushforward of the finite product Gaussian measure under the continuous outer-product sum map; state the scale and integer degrees-of-freedom conventions and retain singular cases.

items.title: A standard-normal matrix with at least as many columns as rows has full row rank almost surely
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $1\le p\le m$ and let $G=[G_1\mid\cdots\mid G_m]$ be a $p\times m$ matrix whose columns are independent $N_p(0,I_p)$ vectors. Then its first $p$ columns are linearly independent almost surely; hence $GG^T$ is positive definite almost surely.
items.strategy: Induct over the first $p$ columns. For each fixed proper span, an independent nondegenerate Gaussian vector lies in it with probability zero because a nonzero orthogonal projection is a continuous scalar normal; use the finite product law to integrate these zero-probability sections.

items.title: The iid multivariate-normal sample and covariance conventions
items.statement: Assume AC and fix integers $n\ge2$, $p\ge1$, $\mu\in\mathbb R^p$, and real symmetric positive-definite $\Sigma$. The observation space is $(\mathbb R^p)^n$ with its finite product Borel sigma-algebra and sampling law $N_p(\mu,\Sigma)^{\otimes n}$. Index $i$ identifies one vector-valued sampling unit, not a scalar coordinate. For observations $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, define $\bar x=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i$, $R=\sum_i(x_i-\bar x)(x_i-\bar x)^T$, the sample covariance $S=R/(n-1)$, and the normalized scatter $M=R/n$. The Gaussian likelihood theorem below, rather than this definition, establishes that $M$ is the maximum-likelihood covariance estimate.
items.strategy: Specify the observation space, parameter labels, product sampling law, sampling unit, and the separate $n-1$ sample-covariance and $n$ normalized-scatter conventions; make no empirical adequacy claim.

items.title: The standard Wishart inverse quadratic form has an exact Fisher law
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $m\ge p\ge1$, let $W\sim W_p(I_p,m)$, and let $Z\sim N_p(0,I_p)$ be independent of $W$. Then $W$ is positive definite almost surely and $\frac{m-p+1}{p}Z^TW^{-1}Z\sim F_{p,m-p+1}$, where the Wishart and Fisher conventions are those defined on this page and in the Gaussian orthogonal-decomposition page.
items.strategy: Represent $W=GG^T$; rotate each fixed direction to the first coordinate using Gaussian orthogonal invariance; a block Schur complement identifies the reciprocal inverse entry with a Gaussian residual squared norm of rank $m-p+1$; combine its chi-square law with the independent $p$-degree Gaussian norm.

items.title: The Gaussian sample mean is independent of the Wishart sample scatter
items.statement: Assume AC and the sample model above. For every $n\ge2$, $\sqrt n(\bar X-\mu)\sim N_p(0,\Sigma)$, $\bar X$ is independent of $S$, and $(n-1)S\sim W_p(\Sigma,n-1)$. If $n>p$, then $S$ is positive definite almost surely. The Wishart scale is $\Sigma$ and its degrees of freedom are $n-1$; the covariance denominator is $n-1$.
items.strategy: Whiten the independent sample vectors and apply one orthogonal transform on the sample-index coordinate whose first row is $n^{-1/2}(1,\ldots,1)$. The first transformed vector gives the mean; the other $n-1$ independent Gaussian vectors give the Wishart scatter. Use the Gaussian-matrix rank lemma only for the $n>p$ invertibility claim.

items.title: The Gaussian covariance likelihood ratio has its fixed-dimensional Wilks limit
items.statement: Assume AC, fix $p\ge1$, and use the iid multivariate-normal sample model with $n>p$. Test $H_0:\Sigma=\Sigma_0$ against unrestricted $\Sigma\in\mathcal S_{++}^p$, with the mean $\mu\in\mathbb R^p$ unrestricted under both hypotheses and fixed $\Sigma_0\succ0$. Let $M=R/n$ be the full-model Gaussian covariance MLE, and let $\Lambda_n$ be the null-over-full maximized likelihood ratio using the explicit Lebesgue Gaussian density. Almost surely, $-2\log\Lambda_n=n[\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_0^{-1}M)-\log\det(\Sigma_0^{-1/2}M\Sigma_0^{-1/2})-p]$. With $p$ fixed and the null true, $-2\log\Lambda_n\Rightarrow\chi^2_{p(p+1)/2}$ as $n\to\infty$. This calibration is asymptotic and uses an interior positive-definite covariance null; no finite-sample chi-square law is asserted.
items.strategy: Derive the explicit product Gaussian likelihood and its unrestricted and constrained maxima. Whiten the sample under the null, apply the multivariate iid CLT to the symmetric second-moment coordinates, expand $x-\log(1+x)-1$ at zero, and identify the limiting quadratic form as the sum of $p(p+1)/2$ independent standard-normal squares.

items.title: The one-sample Hotelling statistic has an exact F law
items.statement: Assume AC, $n>p\ge1$, and the iid multivariate-normal sample model with covariance $\Sigma\succ0$. For $\mu_0\in\mathbb R^p$, define $T^2=n(\bar X-\mu_0)^TS^{-1}(\bar X-\mu_0)$ on $S\succ0$ and set it to $0$ otherwise. Under $H_0:\mu=\mu_0$, $\frac{n-p}{p(n-1)}T^2\sim F_{p,n-p}$. The zero extension does not affect the law because $S\succ0$ almost surely when $n>p$.
items.strategy: Whiten the mean and sample scatter, apply the standard Wishart inverse-quadratic-form lemma with $m=n-1$, and substitute $R=(n-1)S$ to convert its F normalization to the stated sample-covariance convention.

items.title: The exact covariance trace statistic has p(n−1) chi-square degrees of freedom
items.statement: Assume AC, $p\ge1$, $n\ge2$, and the iid multivariate-normal sample model. Under $H_0:\Sigma=\Sigma_0$ for a specified $\Sigma_0\succ0$, the distinct statistic $\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_0^{-1}(n-1)S)$ has the exact law $\chi^2_{p(n-1)}$, even when $n\le p$ and $S$ is singular. This is the Wishart trace statistic, not the covariance likelihood-ratio statistic.
items.strategy: Represent $(n-1)S$ as the Wishart sum of $n-1$ independent $N_p(0,\Sigma_0)$ outer products, whiten each vector by $\Sigma_0^{-1/2}$, and collect all $p(n-1)$ independent squared standard-normal coordinates.

items.title: The one-sample Hotelling F test has exact size alpha
items.statement: Assume AC, $n>p\ge1$, and the model and notation of the exact Hotelling theorem. For $0<\alpha<1$, reject $H_0:\mu=\mu_0$ when $\frac{n-p}{p(n-1)}T^2>F_{p,n-p}^{-1}(1-\alpha)$. The test has size exactly $\alpha$ over all null covariances $\Sigma\succ0$.
items.strategy: The scaled statistic has the common F law under every null parameter; the continuous strictly increasing F CDF supplies the unique upper-tail quantile, so every null rejection probability equals $\alpha$ and their supremum is $\alpha$.

title: Multivariate normal, Wishart, and Hotelling $T^2$ — Examples

items.title: The unbiased sample covariance is singular when 2 ≤ n ≤ p
items.statement: For any $n\ge2$ observations in $\mathbb R^p$ with $2\le n\le p$, their sample covariance $S=(n-1)^{-1}\sum_i(X_i-\bar X)(X_i-\bar X)^T$ is singular. At $n=1$ the stated covariance convention is undefined because its denominator is zero.
items.strategy: Center the data matrix; the all-ones vector is in its kernel, so rank-nullity bounds the centered image by n−1≤p−1. The Gram scatter maps into that proper image and is singular.

items.title: The exact Wishart trace and covariance likelihood ratio are different statistics
items.statement: For $p=1$, $n=4$, $\Sigma_0=1$, and observations $(\sqrt{3/2},-\sqrt{3/2},0,0)$, the sample covariance is $S=1$. The exact trace statistic is $3$, while the covariance likelihood-ratio statistic is $4(\log(4/3)-1/4)\approx0.1507$. This separates the exact $\chi^2_3$ trace calibration from the fixed-dimensional asymptotic $\chi^2_1$ likelihood-ratio calibration; it asserts no finite-sample chi-square law for the latter.
items.strategy: Compute the centered sum of squares, then evaluate the two separately defined statistics using the unbiased covariance and Gaussian maximum-likelihood covariance conventions.

items.title: A two-dimensional Hotelling statistic and its exact F cutoff
items.statement: Assume AC and use the iid multivariate-normal sample model with $p=2$, $n=4$, and fixed positive-definite covariance $\Sigma$. For the observation $x_1=(1,0)^T$, $x_2=(-1,0)^T$, $x_3=(0,1)^T$, and $x_4=(0,-1)^T$, test $H_0:\mu=\mu_0$ with $\mu_0=(1,1)^T$. The sample mean is zero, the sample covariance is $(2/3)I_2$, the Hotelling statistic is $T^2=12$, and its scaled $F_{2,2}$ statistic is $4$. For a chosen $0<\alpha<1$, the exact test rejects precisely when $4>F_{2,2}^{-1}(1-\alpha)$.
items.strategy: Compute the sample mean and covariance from the four vectors, substitute into the Hotelling quadratic form, and apply the exact F calibration with its stated $n-1$ covariance denominator.
